source_slug: 2026-06-15 Telecom Namibia signs more satellite, subsea connectivity deals with Angola firms

fact: Per TechAfrica News, Telecom Namibia (landing party at its Swakopmund landing station) will give Angola Telecom, another operator, an initial dedicated 1 Tbps of capacity on the Equiano cable and host Angola Telecom's equipment there, under a master service agreement signed 12 June 2026.

Telecom Namibia states that Namibia has two subsea cables in service, the existing WACS and Equiano, which it activated on 31 July 2024 at its new Equiano Cable Station in Swakopmund (100G Swakopmund-Johannesburg link); the WACS landing station is not named.
Telecom Namibia states Equiano was co-landed at Swakopmund alongside Paratus, so a second operator (Paratus) holds its own capacity on the cable (minister's remark on collaborative co-landing).

Per Connecting Africa, Telecom Namibia (landing party at its Swakopmund landing station) will give Angola Telecom, another operator, an initial dedicated 1 Tbps of capacity on the Equiano cable and host Angola Telecom's equipment there, under a master service agreement signed 12 June 2026.

Per Telecom Namibia's own release, Telecom Namibia (landing party at its Swakopmund landing station) will give Angola Telecom, another operator, an initial dedicated 1 Tbps of capacity on the Equiano cable and host Angola Telecom's equipment there, under a master service agreement signed 12 June 2026.
An op-ed in Namibian Sun cites Google's Equiano subsea cable, landed at Swakopmund, as Namibia's high-speed link to Europe and the rest of Africa; no other cable is named.

Paratus Group's CEO states Namibia has relied on the WACS cable for its international connectivity until now (June 2022), with Equiano just brought ashore at Swakopmund and expected operational in Q4 2022.
Telecom Namibia's CEO describes leveraging the Equiano subsea cable landing at Swakopmund for Namibia's international bandwidth; no other route is named.
Under an MOU and commercial terms agreement with Telecom Namibia, Angola Telecom will access international capacity through the Equiano cable landing at Swakopmund.

Telecom Namibia states that Namibia has two submarine cables landed, WACS (landed February 2011) and Equiano (landed at Swakopmund on 1 July 2022, projected capacity 4 Tbps), both at Swakopmund so not independent stations.
Data Landscapers states Google's Equiano cable has been operational since 2022 with landings including Namibia (Swakopmund not named in this document).
Paratus's factsheet describes the Swakopmund Equiano cable landing station as operational since Nov 2021, with 2 diverse fibre entry points.

Paratus Namibia says it is the landing partner for the Equiano submarine cable in Namibia, also has access to WACS, and runs its own Trans-Kalahari fibre route from Windhoek to Johannesburg as another route out of the country.
